_about: Hand-edited ledger of machine-transcription garbles (Notion AI, Bloomberg ASR, auto-translation) seen in the archive, with the correct reading. Used by E:\.claude\scripts\transcript_qa.py (source-file scan, page-diff scan) and by ingest_notion_meetings.py (writes a 'Transcription QA' block into every archived Notion file). Keys are matched with word boundaries, case-sensitive unless 'ci' is true. 'keep_when' = regex contexts (same line, ~80 chars around the hit) where the token is legitimate and must NOT be flagged. Add an entry the first time a garble is caught; never delete one. Standing rule (Felipe, 2026-09-28): ALWAYS double-check transcript content — acronyms, names, units, numbers — before it travels to a page.

Smolik.rule: Notion ASR spelling of the Bernstein internet analyst's surname (also 'Schmulich', 'Smollett'); speaker identity still needs the invite.

Mordler.rule: ASR spelling of the Bernstein software analyst's surname.

Amuse.rule: ASR hears 'a Muse' as 'Amuse' in Meta Muse context.

MPO.rule: Notion/Bloomberg ASR hears 'NPO' as 'MPO'. When the token names an optical ARCHITECTURE (opportunity, TAM, ramp, projects, engagements, adoption, laser content, pricing, 'vs CPO', 'inside/outside the box', ELS/faceplate) it is NPO. MPO is only the multi-fibre push-on CONNECTOR (MPO/MTP, '144 MPO connectors', ferrules, US Conec/Senko) or Kolon's MPO resin for CCL.
MPO.first_seen: 2026-08-07 (Jefferies/Curtis LITE call), 2026-08-14 (JPM callback COHR/LITE), 2026-09-28 (JPM Fall Series networking webinar: 63x MPO vs 5x NPO in one transcript; the Notion summary even expanded it to 'Module-Pluggable Optics')

summary_traps: The Notion AI summary inherits every transcript garble AND adds its own: it expanded 'MPO' to 'Module-Pluggable Optics' (2026-09-28), moved a guidance year (fiscal 2025 vs 2028, LITE 2026-09-18), invented a '<15% of industry TAM' sentence (2026-09-18), rendered 'funding short' as 'valuation short' (2026-09-18), hung Meta's $200-300bn figure on AppLovin (2026-09-22), credited the HOST's numbers to the guest (BofA/Bajarin 2026-09-24), and computed its own '~15% CAGR' (Scala 2026-09-24).
Speakers are unlabeled: questions (Capstone/other investors) and answers run together; the host's arithmetic assented with a 'yeah' is not the guest's number.

2026-10-02: Archera/Khanna call - the summary hangs the spoken commitment-growth marks on named clouds (Google 48.5%, AWS 38%, Azure 39.5%); the transcript speaks them as running rates (~45%->48.5% for one cloud, 36.5%->39.5% for another, consumption ~41%) with the cloud named in the surrounding sentence - map each figure to its cloud IN the transcript, never from the summary; the '300-400% mainframe migration volume' is ONE reseller PARTNER's volume (per Khanna), not Archera's total, and '$1 million minimum MAC/PPA' is spoken as a mid-quarter hyperscaler rule for GPU access. AVGO/Arcuri recap - the summary credits Arcuri's relayed statements to Broadcom management and adds 'Jalapeno', 'Sunfish v5', '440s and 430s' that grep does not find in the transcript.
